- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T07:59:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1537
# gh-1537: Retire post-merge main CI — everything gates in the SM pre-merge run

### What changed
- `ci.yml`: dropped `push: branches: [main]` (keeps `tags: v*` + `workflow_dispatch` + the 2h release-coalesce schedule + `release:`). Verified no gate leg keys off push events: the SM validation dispatch runs the whole-tree gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd, app-crap-gate — all full-gate on non-PR events), pinned by a new gate-closure assertion.
- `release-tag` (tag-on-bump) extracted from ci.yml into `release-tag.yml` — it needs a main-push trigger, which ci.yml no longer has; it's release flow, not CI (job fires only on the `chore(release):` bump commit, SM merges skip in ms; the bump's full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which still gates publish/binaries; the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate).
- `release` (bump push) job: dead push arm removed — releases arm on schedule + the two input-gated dispatch arms.
- Flake intake: `flake_watch.py` now filters ci.yml failures to `workflow_dispatch` events (PR-dispatch runs; red tag runs are release-flow failures, triaged by daily-publish/ci-red-report), dedup per test name as before.
- New `sm-merge-guard.yml` + `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py` (AC5): every main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched validation — tree-identity match (fast-forward SHA or squash/merge tree), `chore(release):` bumps skipped; violations file one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue. No nightly backstop.
- Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ci.md describe the single pre-merge gate and the #1522 interaction (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).

### Key decisions
- **Gate closure test** (`test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`): asserts no job in the quality-gate/binaries-smoke-gate needs-closure keys on push events — the release legs (publish, provider smoke, ci-red-report) intentionally key on tag pushes and are outside the closure.
- **Tag extraction over re-triggering**: moving `release-tag` keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow; the App-token wiring, BUMP_SHA pin and enforce-lockfile smoke moved verbatim (existing pins updated, not dropped).
- **Tree sha, not commit sha** in the merge guard: the SM may land fast-forward or squash — the invariant is byte-identical trees.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart \
  test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart \
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[Machine SM serialized queue] -->|update onto main + dispatch ci.yml on head| VAL[Full gate run]
  VAL -->|green| MERGE[Merge: tree lands byte-identical]
  MERGE -->|push main| GUARD[sm-merge-guard.yml]
  GUARD -->|tree covered by a successful dispatch| OK[green]
  GUARD -->|no coverage| ALARM[sm-guard issue]
  BUMP[release job: schedule/dispatch arms] -->|chore(release) push| TAG[release-tag.yml cuts v* tag]
  TAG -->|tag push| TGTRUN[ci.yml v* arm: full gate -> publish/binaries]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).
2. SM (machine-sm/factory-sm): confirm the pre-merge validation dispatch covers EVERY gate that main CI covered, incl. whole-tree crap4dart/coverage/jscpd and the app-crap-gate equivalent; if any gate was main-only, move it into the dispatched run.
3. Flake intake: repoint flake_watch / red-main triage to consume PR-dispatch runs (dedup by test name per #1364 lessons); main-run watching removed together with the trigger.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ updated to describe the single pre-merge gate; note the interaction with #1522 (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).
5. Risk guard, explicit: the invariant is "SM queue is strictly serialized and validates the exact tree being merged". Add a cheap assertion/alarm for its violation (e.g. SM refuses merge if main moved after validation started) instead of relying on nightly backstop.

## Non-goals

- No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly).
- Tags/release CI stays.

Refs: #687 (SM validate-right-before-merge design), #1522 (tag-sourced versions kill release-bot commits), discussion 2026-10-11.

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its

  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

Now I understand the conflict landscape:

**HEAD (PR branch, gh-1537)**: based on pre-#1522 flow — release job pushes a `chore(release):` bump commit to main; release-tag extracted to release-tag.yml; ci.yml drops main-push trigger.

**origin/main**: #1522 landed — release IS the tag; release job cuts tag directly on push to main; no release-bot commits; no release-tag job.

The ticket gh-1537 even says: "together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn". And the PR description's key decision: "Tag extraction over re-triggering: moving release-tag keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow". So the PR branch predates #1522 landing on main. Now that main HAS #1522, the correct resolution is:

- The release job in ci.yml: main's version (#1522 tag-cut flow) wins as the base, BUT the main-push trigger arm question: gh-1537 says drop `push: branches: [main]` from ci.yml. With #1522, the release job's push arm (`push && refs/heads/main`) would never fire if ci.yml doesn't trigger on main pushes. So the release flow arms on schedule + dispatch only — same as gh-1537's HEAD version but with #1522's tag-cut semantics instead of bump-push semantics.

So the correct merge of the release job:
- Comment: combine — gh-1537 (no main-push arm; releases arm on the 2h coalesce schedule + gated dispatches) + gh-1522 (the release IS the tag).
- `if:` condition: drop the push arm, keep schedule + dispatch arms. So: `(github.event_name == 'schedule' || (workflow_dispatch && releaseDryRun) || (workflow_dispatch && main && releaseDispatch))`.

# gh-1537 — the tag-on-bump phase of the release chain, extracted from
# ci.yml. It needs a push-to-main trigger, and ci.yml no longer has one:
# the post-merge main CI run is retired (the SM's pre-merge validation
# dispatch is the single CI gate). THIS FILE IS RELEASE FLOW, NOT CI —
# it runs no validation gates:
#   - the only push that starts the job is the fa-release-bot App's
#     'chore(release):' bump commit (gh-1172 direct push to protected
#     main) — SM merge commits (squash subjects `KEY summary (#PR)`)
#     evaluate the job `if` to false and skip in milliseconds,
#   - the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate (gh-1299 NG2/AC3,
#     pinned by release_hygiene_test.dart — inside tag_release.sh),
#   - the FULL quality gate runs on the cut v* tag (ci.yml's tags arm)
#     BEFORE publish/binaries — the bump commit's validation moved there.
# Serialized with the ci.yml bump job via the release-main group: tag
# first, next bump after. (#1522 will retire the bump flow itself once
# tag-sourced versions land — this workflow goes with it.)
name: Release tag

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the pushed 'chore(release):'
  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,
  # next bump after. gh-1537: extracted from ci.yml (no main-push trigger
  # there anymore) and dropped the needs: quality-gate — the bump commit's
  # full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which gates
  # publish/binaries (see the file header).
  release-tag:
    name: Auto-release (tag on push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      # Same fa-release-bot App as the bump job (gh-1172): the tag push and
      # `gh release create` ride the App installation token — without an
      # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in tag_release.sh was a
      # guaranteed silent no-op and the curated CHANGELOG notes never reached
      # the release object (BLOCK finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write only —

## PR Description

Closes #1537
# gh-1537: Retire post-merge main CI — everything gates in the SM pre-merge run

### What changed
- `ci.yml`: dropped `push: branches: [main]` (keeps `tags: v*` + `workflow_dispatch` + the 2h release-coalesce schedule + `release:`). Verified no gate leg keys off push events: the SM validation dispatch runs the whole-tree gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd, app-crap-gate — all full-gate on non-PR events), pinned by a new gate-closure assertion.
- `release-tag` (tag-on-bump) extracted from ci.yml into `release-tag.yml` — it needs a main-push trigger, which ci.yml no longer has; it's release flow, not CI (job fires only on the `chore(release):` bump commit, SM merges skip in ms; the bump's full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which still gates publish/binaries; the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate).
- `release` (bump push) job: dead push arm removed — releases arm on schedule + the two input-gated dispatch arms.
- Flake intake: `flake_watch.py` now filters ci.yml failures to `workflow_dispatch` events (PR-dispatch runs; red tag runs are release-flow failures, triaged by daily-publish/ci-red-report), dedup per test name as before.
- New `sm-merge-guard.yml` + `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py` (AC5): every main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched validation — tree-identity match (fast-forward SHA or squash/merge tree), `chore(release):` bumps skipped; violations file one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue. No nightly backstop.
- Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ci.md describe the single pre-merge gate and the #1522 interaction (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).

### Key decisions
- **Gate closure test** (`test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`): asserts no job in the quality-gate/binaries-smoke-gate needs-closure keys on push events — the release legs (publish, provider smoke, ci-red-report) intentionally key on tag pushes and are outside the closure.
- **Tag extraction over re-triggering**: moving `release-tag` keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow; the App-token wiring, BUMP_SHA pin and enforce-lockfile smoke moved verbatim (existing pins updated, not dropped).
- **Tree sha, not commit sha** in the merge guard: the SM may land fast-forward or squash — the invariant is byte-identical trees.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart \
  test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart \
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[Machine SM serialized queue] -->|update onto main + dispatch ci.yml on head| VAL[Full gate run]
  VAL -->|green| MERGE[Merge: tree lands byte-identical]
  MERGE -->|push main| GUARD[sm-merge-guard.yml]
  GUARD -->|tree covered by a successful dispatch| OK[green]
  GUARD -->|no coverage| ALARM[sm-guard issue]
  BUMP[release job: schedule/dispatch arms] -->|chore(release) push| TAG[release-tag.yml cuts v* tag]
  TAG -->|tag push| TGTRUN[ci.yml v* arm: full gate -> publish/binaries]
```

</details>

# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).
2. SM (machine-sm/factory-sm): confirm the pre-merge validation dispatch covers EVERY gate that main CI covered, incl. whole-tree crap4dart/coverage/jscpd and the app-crap-gate equivalent; if any gate was main-only, move it into the dispatched run.
3. Flake intake: repoint flake_watch / red-main triage to consume PR-dispatch runs (dedup by test name per #1364 lessons); main-run watching removed together with the trigger.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ updated to describe the single pre-merge gate; note the interaction with #1522 (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).
5. Risk guard, explicit: the invariant is "SM queue is strictly serialized and validates the exact tree being merged". Add a cheap assertion/alarm for its violation (e.g. SM refuses merge if main moved after validation started) instead of relying on nightly backstop.

## Non-goals

- No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly).
- Tags/release CI stays.

Refs: #687 (SM validate-right-before-merge design), #1522 (tag-sourced versions kill release-bot commits), discussion 2026-10-11.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:

## PR Description

Closes #1537
# gh-1537: Retire post-merge main CI — everything gates in the SM pre-merge run

### What changed
- `ci.yml`: dropped `push: branches: [main]` (keeps `tags: v*` + `workflow_dispatch` + the 2h release-coalesce schedule + `release:`). Verified no gate leg keys off push events: the SM validation dispatch runs the whole-tree gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd, app-crap-gate — all full-gate on non-PR events), pinned by a new gate-closure assertion.
- `release-tag` (tag-on-bump) extracted from ci.yml into `release-tag.yml` — it needs a main-push trigger, which ci.yml no longer has; it's release flow, not CI (job fires only on the `chore(release):` bump commit, SM merges skip in ms; the bump's full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which still gates publish/binaries; the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate).
- `release` (bump push) job: dead push arm removed — releases arm on schedule + the two input-gated dispatch arms.
- Flake intake: `flake_watch.py` now filters ci.yml failures to `workflow_dispatch` events (PR-dispatch runs; red tag runs are release-flow failures, triaged by daily-publish/ci-red-report), dedup per test name as before.
- New `sm-merge-guard.yml` + `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py` (AC5): every main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched validation — tree-identity match (fast-forward SHA or squash/merge tree), `chore(release):` bumps skipped; violations file one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue. No nightly backstop.
- Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ci.md describe the single pre-merge gate and the #1522 interaction (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).

### Key decisions
- **Gate closure test** (`test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`): asserts no job in the quality-gate/binaries-smoke-gate needs-closure keys on push events — the release legs (publish, provider smoke, ci-red-report) intentionally key on tag pushes and are outside the closure.
- **Tag extraction over re-triggering**: moving `release-tag` keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow; the App-token wiring, BUMP_SHA pin and enforce-lockfile smoke moved verbatim (existing pins updated, not dropped).
- **Tree sha, not commit sha** in the merge guard: the SM may land fast-forward or squash — the invariant is byte-identical trees.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart \
  test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart \
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[Machine SM serialized queue] -->|update onto main + dispatch ci.yml on head| VAL[Full gate run]
  VAL -->|green| MERGE[Merge: tree lands byte-identical]
  MERGE -->|push main| GUARD[sm-merge-guard.yml]
  GUARD -->|tree covered by a successful dispatch| OK[green]
  GUARD -->|no coverage| ALARM[sm-guard issue]
  BUMP[release job: schedule/dispatch arms] -->|chore(release) push| TAG[release-tag.yml cuts v* tag]
  TAG -->|tag push| TGTRUN[ci.yml v* arm: full gate -> publish/binaries]
```

</details>

# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).
2. SM (machine-sm/factory-sm): confirm the pre-merge validation dispatch covers EVERY gate that main CI covered, incl. whole-tree crap4dart/coverage/jscpd and the app-crap-gate equivalent; if any gate was main-only, move it into the dispatched run.
3. Flake intake: repoint flake_watch / red-main triage to consume PR-dispatch runs (dedup by test name per #1364 lessons); main-run watching removed together with the trigger.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ updated to describe the single pre-merge gate; note the interaction with #1522 (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).
5. Risk guard, explicit: the invariant is "SM queue is strictly serialized and validates the exact tree being merged". Add a cheap assertion/alarm for its violation (e.g. SM refuses merge if main moved after validation started) instead of relying on nightly backstop.

## Non-goals

- No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly).
- Tags/release CI stays.

Refs: #687 (SM validate-right-before-merge design), #1522 (tag-sourced versions kill release-bot commits), discussion 2026-10-11.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:

## PR Description

Closes #1537
# gh-1537: Retire post-merge main CI — everything gates in the SM pre-merge run

### What changed
- `ci.yml`: dropped `push: branches: [main]` (keeps `tags: v*` + `workflow_dispatch` + the 2h release-coalesce schedule + `release:`). Verified no gate leg keys off push events: the SM validation dispatch runs the whole-tree gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd, app-crap-gate — all full-gate on non-PR events), pinned by a new gate-closure assertion.
- `release-tag` (tag-on-bump) extracted from ci.yml into `release-tag.yml` — it needs a main-push trigger, which ci.yml no longer has; it's release flow, not CI (job fires only on the `chore(release):` bump commit, SM merges skip in ms; the bump's full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which still gates publish/binaries; the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate).
- `release` (bump push) job: dead push arm removed — releases arm on schedule + the two input-gated dispatch arms.
- Flake intake: `flake_watch.py` now filters ci.yml failures to `workflow_dispatch` events (PR-dispatch runs; red tag runs are release-flow failures, triaged by daily-publish/ci-red-report), dedup per test name as before.
- New `sm-merge-guard.yml` + `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py` (AC5): every main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched validation — tree-identity match (fast-forward SHA or squash/merge tree), `chore(release):` bumps skipped; violations file one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue. No nightly backstop.
- Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ci.md describe the single pre-merge gate and the #1522 interaction (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).

### Key decisions
- **Gate closure test** (`test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`): asserts no job in the quality-gate/binaries-smoke-gate needs-closure keys on push events — the release legs (publish, provider smoke, ci-red-report) intentionally key on tag pushes and are outside the closure.
- **Tag extraction over re-triggering**: moving `release-tag` keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow; the App-token wiring, BUMP_SHA pin and enforce-lockfile smoke moved verbatim (existing pins updated, not dropped).
- **Tree sha, not commit sha** in the merge guard: the SM may land fast-forward or squash — the invariant is byte-identical trees.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart \
  test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart \
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[Machine SM serialized queue] -->|update onto main + dispatch ci.yml on head| VAL[Full gate run]
  VAL -->|green| MERGE[Merge: tree lands byte-identical]
  MERGE -->|push main| GUARD[sm-merge-guard.yml]
  GUARD -->|tree covered by a successful dispatch| OK[green]
  GUARD -->|no coverage| ALARM[sm-guard issue]
  BUMP[release job: schedule/dispatch arms] -->|chore(release) push| TAG[release-tag.yml cuts v* tag]
  TAG -->|tag push| TGTRUN[ci.yml v* arm: full gate -> publish/binaries]
```

</details>

# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).
2. SM (machine-sm/factory-sm): confirm the pre-merge validation dispatch covers EVERY gate that main CI covered, incl. whole-tree crap4dart/coverage/jscpd and the app-crap-gate equivalent; if any gate was main-only, move it into the dispatched run.
3. Flake intake: repoint flake_watch / red-main triage to consume PR-dispatch runs (dedup by test name per #1364 lessons); main-run watching removed together with the trigger.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ updated to describe the single pre-merge gate; note the interaction with #1522 (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).
5. Risk guard, explicit: the invariant is "SM queue is strictly serialized and validates the exact tree being merged". Add a cheap assertion/alarm for its violation (e.g. SM refuses merge if main moved after validation started) instead of relying on nightly backstop.

## Non-goals

- No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly).
- Tags/release CI stays.

Refs: #687 (SM validate-right-before-merge design), #1522 (tag-sourced versions kill release-bot commits), discussion 2026-10-11.

blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:

# the post-merge main CI run is retired (the SM's pre-merge validation

permissions:

jobs:

  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,

## PR Description

Closes #1537
# gh-1537: Retire post-merge main CI — everything gates in the SM pre-merge run

### What changed
- `ci.yml`: dropped `push: branches: [main]` (keeps `tags: v*` + `workflow_dispatch` + the 2h release-coalesce schedule + `release:`). Verified no gate leg keys off push events: the SM validation dispatch runs the whole-tree gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd, app-crap-gate — all full-gate on non-PR events), pinned by a new gate-closure assertion.
- `release-tag` (tag-on-bump) extracted from ci.yml into `release-tag.yml` — it needs a main-push trigger, which ci.yml no longer has; it's release flow, not CI (job fires only on the `chore(release):` bump commit, SM merges skip in ms; the bump's full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which still gates publish/binaries; the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate).
- `release` (bump push) job: dead push arm removed — releases arm on schedule + the two input-gated dispatch arms.
- Flake intake: `flake_watch.py` now filters ci.yml failures to `workflow_dispatch` events (PR-dispatch runs; red tag runs are release-flow failures, triaged by daily-publish/ci-red-report), dedup per test name as before.
- New `sm-merge-guard.yml` + `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py` (AC5): every main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched validation — tree-identity match (fast-forward SHA or squash/merge tree), `chore(release):` bumps skipped; violations file one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue. No nightly backstop.
- Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ci.md describe the single pre-merge gate and the #1522 interaction (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).

### Key decisions
- **Gate closure test** (`test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`): asserts no job in the quality-gate/binaries-smoke-gate needs-closure keys on push events — the release legs (publish, provider smoke, ci-red-report) intentionally key on tag pushes and are outside the closure.
- **Tag extraction over re-triggering**: moving `release-tag` keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow; the App-token wiring, BUMP_SHA pin and enforce-lockfile smoke moved verbatim (existing pins updated, not dropped).
- **Tree sha, not commit sha** in the merge guard: the SM may land fast-forward or squash — the invariant is byte-identical trees.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart \
  test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart \
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[Machine SM serialized queue] -->|update onto main + dispatch ci.yml on head| VAL[Full gate run]
  VAL -->|green| MERGE[Merge: tree lands byte-identical]
  MERGE -->|push main| GUARD[sm-merge-guard.yml]
  GUARD -->|tree covered by a successful dispatch| OK[green]
  GUARD -->|no coverage| ALARM[sm-guard issue]
  BUMP[release job: schedule/dispatch arms] -->|chore(release) push| TAG[release-tag.yml cuts v* tag]
  TAG -->|tag push| TGTRUN[ci.yml v* arm: full gate -> publish/binaries]
```

</details>

# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`

  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:

# gh-1537 — the tag-on-bump phase of the release chain, extracted from
# ci.yml. It needs a push-to-main trigger, and ci.yml no longer has one:
# the post-merge main CI run is retired (the SM's pre-merge validation
# dispatch is the single CI gate). THIS FILE IS RELEASE FLOW, NOT CI —
# it runs no validation gates:
#   - the only push that starts the job is the fa-release-bot App's
#     'chore(release):' bump commit (gh-1172 direct push to protected
#     main) — SM merge commits (squash subjects `KEY summary (#PR)`)
#     evaluate the job `if` to false and skip in milliseconds,
#   - the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate (gh-1299 NG2/AC3,
#     pinned by release_hygiene_test.dart — inside tag_release.sh),
#   - the FULL quality gate runs on the cut v* tag (ci.yml's tags arm)
#     BEFORE publish/binaries — the bump commit's validation moved there.
# Serialized with the ci.yml bump job via the release-main group: tag
# first, next bump after. (#1522 will retire the bump flow itself once
# tag-sourced versions land — this workflow goes with it.)
name: Release tag

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the pushed 'chore(release):'
  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,
  # next bump after. gh-1537: extracted from ci.yml (no main-push trigger
  # there anymore) and dropped the needs: quality-gate — the bump commit's
  # full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which gates
  # publish/binaries (see the file header).
  release-tag:
    name: Auto-release (tag on push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      # Same fa-release-bot App as the bump job (gh-1172): the tag push and
      # `gh release create` ride the App installation token — without an
      # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in tag_release.sh was a
      # guaranteed silent no-op and the curated CHANGELOG notes never reached
      # the release object (BLOCK finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write only —

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1541
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1541
- **Title**: gh-1537 [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1537` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -119
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T07:42:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T07:59:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1537
# gh-1537: Retire post-merge main CI — everything gates in the SM pre-merge run

### What changed
- `ci.yml`: dropped `push: branches: [main]` (keeps `tags: v*` + `workflow_dispatch` + the 2h release-coalesce schedule + `release:`). Verified no gate leg keys off push events: the SM validation dispatch runs the whole-tree gates (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd, app-crap-gate — all full-gate on non-PR events), pinned by a new gate-closure assertion.
- `release-tag` (tag-on-bump) extracted from ci.yml into `release-tag.yml` — it needs a main-push trigger, which ci.yml no longer has; it's release flow, not CI (job fires only on the `chore(release):` bump commit, SM merges skip in ms; the bump's full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which still gates publish/binaries; the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate).
- `release` (bump push) job: dead push arm removed — releases arm on schedule + the two input-gated dispatch arms.
- Flake intake: `flake_watch.py` now filters ci.yml failures to `workflow_dispatch` events (PR-dispatch runs; red tag runs are release-flow failures, triaged by daily-publish/ci-red-report), dedup per test name as before.
- New `sm-merge-guard.yml` + `scripts/sm_merge_guard.py` (AC5): every main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched validation — tree-identity match (fast-forward SHA or squash/merge tree), `chore(release):` bumps skipped; violations file one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue. No nightly backstop.
- Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ci.md describe the single pre-merge gate and the #1522 interaction (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).

### Key decisions
- **Gate closure test** (`test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`): asserts no job in the quality-gate/binaries-smoke-gate needs-closure keys on push events — the release legs (publish, provider smoke, ci-red-report) intentionally key on tag pushes and are outside the closure.
- **Tag extraction over re-triggering**: moving `release-tag` keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow; the App-token wiring, BUMP_SHA pin and enforce-lockfile smoke moved verbatim (existing pins updated, not dropped).
- **Tree sha, not commit sha** in the merge guard: the SM may land fast-forward or squash — the invariant is byte-identical trees.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart test/scripts/sm_merge_guard_test.dart \
  test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart \
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[Machine SM serialized queue] -->|update onto main + dispatch ci.yml on head| VAL[Full gate run]
  VAL -->|green| MERGE[Merge: tree lands byte-identical]
  MERGE -->|push main| GUARD[sm-merge-guard.yml]
  GUARD -->|tree covered by a successful dispatch| OK[green]
  GUARD -->|no coverage| ALARM[sm-guard issue]
  BUMP[release job: schedule/dispatch arms] -->|chore(release) push| TAG[release-tag.yml cuts v* tag]
  TAG -->|tag push| TGTRUN[ci.yml v* arm: full gate -> publish/binaries]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).
2. SM (machine-sm/factory-sm): confirm the pre-merge validation dispatch covers EVERY gate that main CI covered, incl. whole-tree crap4dart/coverage/jscpd and the app-crap-gate equivalent; if any gate was main-only, move it into the dispatched run.
3. Flake intake: repoint flake_watch / red-main triage to consume PR-dispatch runs (dedup by test name per #1364 lessons); main-run watching removed together with the trigger.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ updated to describe the single pre-merge gate; note the interaction with #1522 (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).
5. Risk guard, explicit: the invariant is "SM queue is strictly serialized and validates the exact tree being merged". Add a cheap assertion/alarm for its violation (e.g. SM refuses merge if main moved after validation started) instead of relying on nightly backstop.

## Non-goals

- No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly).
- Tags/release CI stays.

Refs: #687 (SM validate-right-before-merge design), #1522 (tag-sourced versions kill release-bot commits), discussion 2026-10-11.
