blocks.text:
release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:

Now I understand the conflict landscape:

**HEAD (PR branch, gh-1537)**: based on pre-#1522 flow — release job pushes a `chore(release):` bump commit to main; release-tag extracted to release-tag.yml; ci.yml drops main-push trigger.

**origin/main**: #1522 landed — release IS the tag; release job cuts tag directly on push to main; no release-bot commits; no release-tag job.

The ticket gh-1537 even says: "together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn". And the PR description's key decision: "Tag extraction over re-triggering: moving release-tag keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow". So the PR branch predates #1522 landing on main. Now that main HAS #1522, the correct resolution is:

- The release job in ci.yml: main's version (#1522 tag-cut flow) wins as the base, BUT the main-push trigger arm question: gh-1537 says drop `push: branches: [main]` from ci.yml. With #1522, the release job's push arm (`push && refs/heads/main`) would never fire if ci.yml doesn't trigger on main pushes. So the release flow arms on schedule + dispatch only — same as gh-1537's HEAD version but with #1522's tag-cut semantics instead of bump-push semantics.

So the correct merge of the release job:
- Comment: combine — gh-1537 (no main-push arm; releases arm on the 2h coalesce schedule + gated dispatches) + gh-1522 (the release IS the tag).
- `if:` condition: drop the push arm, keep schedule + dispatch arms. So: `(github.event_name == 'schedule' || (workflow_dispatch && releaseDryRun) || (workflow_dispatch && main && releaseDispatch))`.
- Steps: main's version (token mint, checkout, "Cut release tag + GitHub Release" with GH_TOKEN). No python/flutter setup (that was for the bump regenerating lockfiles — #1522 retired the bump commit). No release-tag.yml extraction since main has no release-tag job and no bump commit.
- Keep the main's "Cut release tag" step and remove HEAD's flutter/python bump steps.
- Also drop the "release-tag lives in release-tag.yml" comment block after the release job.

Also check: does the PR branch still have `release-tag.yml` workflow and `sm-merge-guard.yml`, `sm_merge_guard.py`, `flake_watch.py` changes, `test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`? Those are additive from HEAD. But if #1522 landed, the PR's release-tag.yml (tag-on-bump) is obsolete. The PR description says "moving release-tag keeps the release chain working until #1522 retires the bump flow" — #1522 has now landed, so release-tag.yml should probably be DROPPED. # gh-1537 — the tag-on-bump phase of the release chain, extracted from
# ci.yml. It needs a push-to-main trigger, and ci.yml no longer has one:
# the post-merge main CI run is retired (the SM's pre-merge validation
# dispatch is the single CI gate). THIS FILE IS RELEASE FLOW, NOT CI —
# it runs no validation gates:
#   - the only push that starts the job is the fa-release-bot App's
#     'chore(release):' bump commit (gh-1172 direct push to protected
#     main) — SM merge commits (squash subjects `KEY summary (#PR)`)
#     evaluate the job `if` to false and skip in milliseconds,
#   - the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate (gh-1299 NG2/AC3,
#     pinned by release_hygiene_test.dart — inside tag_release.sh),
#   - the FULL quality gate runs on the cut v* tag (ci.yml's tags arm)
#     BEFORE publish/binaries — the bump commit's validation moved there.
# Serialized with the ci.yml bump job via the release-main group: tag
# first, next bump after. (#1522 will retire the bump flow itself once
# tag-sourced versions land — this workflow goes with it.)
name: Release tag

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the pushed 'chore(release):'
  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,
  # next bump after. gh-1537: extracted from ci.yml (no main-push trigger
  # there anymore) and dropped the needs: quality-gate — the bump commit's
  # full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which gates
  # publish/binaries (see the file header).
  release-tag:
    name: Auto-release (tag on push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      # Same fa-release-bot App as the bump job (gh-1172): the tag push and
      # `gh release create` ride the App installation token — without an
      # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in tag_release.sh was a
      # guaranteed silent no-op and the curated CHANGELOG notes never reached
      # the release object (BLOCK finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write only —

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be

# gh-1537 — the tag-on-bump phase of the release chain, extracted from
# ci.yml. It needs a push-to-main trigger, and ci.yml no longer has one:
# the post-merge main CI run is retired (the SM's pre-merge validation
# dispatch is the single CI gate). THIS FILE IS RELEASE FLOW, NOT CI —
# it runs no validation gates:
#   - the only push that starts the job is the fa-release-bot App's
#     'chore(release):' bump commit (gh-1172 direct push to protected
#     main) — SM merge commits (squash subjects `KEY summary (#PR)`)
#     evaluate the job `if` to false and skip in milliseconds,
#   - the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate (gh-1299 NG2/AC3,
#     pinned by release_hygiene_test.dart — inside tag_release.sh),
#   - the FULL quality gate runs on the cut v* tag (ci.yml's tags arm)
#     BEFORE publish/binaries — the bump commit's validation moved there.
# Serialized with the ci.yml bump job via the release-main group: tag
# first, next bump after. (#1522 will retire the bump flow itself once
# tag-sourced versions land — this workflow goes with it.)
name: Release tag

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the pushed 'chore(release):'
  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,
  # next bump after. gh-1537: extracted from ci.yml (no main-push trigger
  # there anymore) and dropped the needs: quality-gate — the bump commit's
  # full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which gates
  # publish/binaries (see the file header).
  release-tag:
    name: Auto-release (tag on push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      # Same fa-release-bot App as the bump job (gh-1172): the tag push and
      # `gh release create` ride the App installation token — without an
      # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in tag_release.sh was a
      # guaranteed silent no-op and the curated CHANGELOG notes never reached
      # the release object (BLOCK finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write only —

# ci.yml. It needs a push-to-main trigger, and ci.yml no longer has one:
# the post-merge main CI run is retired (the SM's pre-merge validation
# dispatch is the single CI gate). THIS FILE IS RELEASE FLOW, NOT CI —
# it runs no validation gates:
#   - the only push that starts the job is the fa-release-bot App's
#     'chore(release):' bump commit (gh-1172 direct push to protected
#     main) — SM merge commits (squash subjects `KEY summary (#PR)`)
#     evaluate the job `if` to false and skip in milliseconds,
#   - the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate (gh-1299 NG2/AC3,
#     pinned by release_hygiene_test.dart — inside tag_release.sh),
#   - the FULL quality gate runs on the cut v* tag (ci.yml's tags arm)
#     BEFORE publish/binaries — the bump commit's validation moved there.
# Serialized with the ci.yml bump job via the release-main group: tag
# first, next bump after. (#1522 will retire the bump flow itself once
# tag-sourced versions land — this workflow goes with it.)
name: Release tag

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the pushed 'chore(release):'
  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,
  # next bump after. gh-1537: extracted from ci.yml (no main-push trigger
  # there anymore) and dropped the needs: quality-gate — the bump commit's
  # full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which gates
  # publish/binaries (see the file header).
  release-tag:
    name: Auto-release (tag on push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main

    permissions:
      contents: write

        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

# gh-1537 — the tag-on-bump phase of the release chain, extracted from
# ci.yml. It needs a push-to-main trigger, and ci.yml no longer has one:
# the post-merge main CI run is retired (the SM's pre-merge validation
# dispatch is the single CI gate). THIS FILE IS RELEASE FLOW, NOT CI —
# it runs no validation gates:
#   - the only push that starts the job is the fa-release-bot App's
#     'chore(release):' bump commit (gh-1172 direct push to protected
#     main) — SM merge commits (squash subjects `KEY summary (#PR)`)
#     evaluate the job `if` to false and skip in milliseconds,
#   - the enforce-lockfile smoke stays the pre-tag gate (gh-1299 NG2/AC3,
#     pinned by release_hygiene_test.dart — inside tag_release.sh),
#   - the FULL quality gate runs on the cut v* tag (ci.yml's tags arm)
#     BEFORE publish/binaries — the bump commit's validation moved there.
# Serialized with the ci.yml bump job via the release-main group: tag
# first, next bump after. (#1522 will retire the bump flow itself once
# tag-sourced versions land — this workflow goes with it.)
name: Release tag

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the pushed 'chore(release):'
  # bump commit (see scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump lands via direct push
  # to protected main as the fa-release-bot App (gh-1172), so the tag phase
  # keys on that push. Tag push rides the App token (checkout token) —
  # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
  # Serialized with the bump push job via the release-main group: tag first,
  # next bump after. gh-1537: extracted from ci.yml (no main-push trigger
  # there anymore) and dropped the needs: quality-gate — the bump commit's
  # full-gate validation moved to the cut v* tag run, which gates
  # publish/binaries (see the file header).
  release-tag:
    name: Auto-release (tag on push)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      # Same fa-release-bot App as the bump job (gh-1172): the tag push and
      # `gh release create` ride the App installation token — without an
      # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in tag_release.sh was a
      # guaranteed silent no-op and the curated CHANGELOG notes never reached
      # the release object (BLOCK finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write only —

content.text:
`workflow_dispatch` input `legs` selects a single leg (`all` by default) —
the safe way to smoke one channel.

## Versioning

The scheme (gh-1522): the git TAG is the single source of truth —
`scripts/auto_release.sh` cuts an annotated tag (latest tag + 1) directly
on `origin/main` plus the GitHub Release, authenticated as the fa-release-bot
GitHub App (gh-1172 — its token triggers the tag-scoped jobs, which
`GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes never do). ZERO commits land on main: the retired
....
`releaseDispatch`) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag → watch
the tag-scoped `publish`/`binaries` jobs. The daily:

- lets `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` derive their version
  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;
- keeps NO daily-side wedge alarm for a tag that never publishes (#1368):
  a freshly cut tag reads `release-in-flight` ⏭️ in the daily for as long

content.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

- lets `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` derive their version
  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag

- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;

# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \

issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
====
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard: the
bump commit is authored by the gated release job itself and is gated
downstream — tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, and the
full quality gate runs on the v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.

blocks.text:
# gh-1537 AC5 — the cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation
# invariant. With the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing else stands
# between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly serialized and
# validates the exact tree being merged", #687) and a red main: this
# workflow fires on EVERY push to main and asserts the pushed tree was
# covered by a successful ci.yml workflow_dispatch run — the SM's
# pre-merge validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# The release-bot's chore(release) bump pushes skip the guard (the v* tag
# run gates them: tag_release.sh's enforce-lockfile smoke pre-tag, the
# full quality gate on the tag before publish). SM merge commits and any
# human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so both fast-forward
# (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree) landings validate.
name: SM merge guard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The pushed head is the checked-out HEAD; only its tree sha is
          # read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can drift
          # to a main that moved in the seconds before the job starts
          # (same lesson as the ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 scripts/sm_merge_guard.py \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
